title: Pulse-and-decay commit simulator (stress hypotheses)
content:
Purpose:
This sheet captures a compact, reproducible stress-test harness for reserved GPU pool economics under short-term demand pulses and multi-customer commit decay. The goal is to understand how transient spikes, staggered churn, and concentrated cohort migrations affect days-of-runway, marginal unit cost, and recommended buffer sizing for committed pools.

High-level questions we want answered:
- If 3 large customers (10–20% of pool) reduce committed utilization by 50% over 60 days, what is the pool-level utilization and net daily burn?
- How many days of committed buffer (or burst credits) needed to keep SLO-level throughput at 95% coverage versus a model-fallback strategy?
- What is the marginal cost per effective vGPU-hour when we reallocate spare capacity to spot / shared customers vs. leaving idle?

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Dedicated/reserved pools (monthly/annual commits). Scenario-driven simulation, no infra-level latency modeling.
- Non-goal: Not a pricing change recommendation in isolation; it feeds into pricing experiments.

Key assumptions (editable by parameter tab):
- Pool size (vGPU-equivalent): default 200 vGPU-hours/day capacity.
- Committed baseline utilization: 78% (i.e., committed workloads consume 78% of provisioned capacity on avg).
- Credit-bucket (burst credits) size per pool: default 40 vGPU-hours/day for 14 days.
- Customer cohort sizes: small(<=1%), medium(1-5%), large(5-20%).
- Churn types: pulse (sharp drop/raise over 3–7 days), decay (linear decline over 30–90 days), migration (instant drop when customers switch).
- Price arithmetic: hosted spot revenue per vGPU-hour: $X (parameter); committed amortized cost per vGPU-hour: $Y.

Methodology overview:
1) Parameter tab: all knobs (pool size, initial utilization, cohort distribution, churn velocity, spot price, amortized commit cost, burst credit rules).
2) Scenario generator: monte-carlo-like enumerator that combines churn types across cohorts. For lightweight sheet, we enumerate deterministic combos (base / +pulse-50% / +decay-30%-90d / mass-migration 15%).
3) Day-by-day simulation tab: for each scenario, compute per-day demand, apply cache/burst rules, compute utilization, idle capacity, and revenue salvage rate (if we reassign to spot customers).
4) Metrics tab: compute moving-average utilization, days-to-breach (coverage < target), marginal-cost-per-served-token, and recommended buffer in days and vGPU-hours.

Sheet layout (tabs):
- PARAMS: single-row key/value controls for all assumptions.
- COHORTS: one line per customer cohort with committed vGPU-hours, churn profile, priority tier, migration probability. Columns: Cohort, Committed-hours/day, Fraction-of-pool, Churn-type, Churn-start-day, Churn-length-days, Migration-prob.
- SCENARIO-DEFS: list of named scenarios and pointers to cohort changes.
- DAILY-SIM-[scenario name]: date, demand_raw_vGPUh, demand_after_cache, burst_applied, spot_assigned, idle_vGPUh, utilization_pct, amortized_cost, salvage_revenue, net_burn_usd.
- METRICS: summary rows for scenario -> coverage-days (days until utilization < target), avg-utilization, peak-idle, worst-day-net-burn, marginal-cost-per-vGPUh.
- SENSITIVITY: small tables showing effect of varying burst credit size and spot salvage rate on days-to-breach.

Key formulas / canonical cells (sheet-friendly versions):
- daily_utilization_pct = (demand_after_cache - spot_assigned) / pool_capacity
- idle_vGPUh = max(0, pool_capacity - demand_after_cache)
- burst_applied = min(burst_remaining, demand_spike_amount)
- net_burn_usd = amortized_commit_cost * pool_capacity - salvage_revenue - spot_rev_from_uncommitted

Example tiny scenario excerpt (CSV-like) for "pulse-50pct-large-cohort" tab header:
Date,raw_demand_vGPUh,after_cache,burst_used,spot_assigned,idle_vGPUh,util_pct,net_burn_usd
2026-01-01,156,150,0,0,50,75%,$1,240
2026-01-02,80,78,20,0,102,39%,$980
2026-01-03,38,36,14,0,144,18%,$1,150
...

Scenario descriptions (examples):
- BASE: no churn, baseline utilization 78%, burst credits unused.
- SHORT-PULSE: large cohort reduces usage by 50% for 7 days starting day 10 then returns.
- SLOW-DECAY: medium cohort decays 30% linearly across 60 days.
- MIGRATION-WAVE: 3 large customers migrate away across a 21-day window (staggered drops 5%, 7%, 8%).
- COMBO-TAIL-RISK: SHORT-PULSE + SLOW-DECAY + spot-price drop (reduces salvage revenue by 40%).

Preliminary results summary (quick takeaways from initial runs with default params):
- Short pulses (7 days) created a temporary utilization drop to ~42% on worst days; with default 14-day burst bucket the pool remained cashflow-positive but idle increased avg by ~22 vGPUh/day.
- Slow decay of a medium cohort (30% over 60 days) reduces avg utilization by ~9 p.p.; Marginal cost per served vGPUh increases 9–14% unless we aggressively reprice or move idle to spot customers.
- Migration wave (three large customers) leads to a 12–20 day window where pool utilization sits below 55% and net burn increases by ~18% relative to baseline.

Actionable recommendations (draft):
1) Implement a lightweight detection trigger: if pool-level utilization < 60% for 7 consecutive days, open a temporary spot-offer lane and discount spot by X% to attract short-term demand. Measure salvage rate over 14 days.
2) For customers in large cohorts, include a quarterly churn-forecast clause in renewals (with incentives to smooth rampdown) — reduce tail-risk by stabilizing commit end-dates.
3) Reserve a policy of minimum buffer = max(14 days, 10% pool capacity) to handle combined pulse+decay risks; link to dedicated-ui toggle for buffer resizing.
4) Run price experiments for salvage revenue: test spot discounts {10%, 25%, 40%} and track fill rate and marginal cost.

Open questions / uncertainties:
- Salvage elasticity: how much does a 10% spot discount increase fill rate in real demand? Need empirical test.
- Cache interactions: we assume prefix caching reduces new demand by fixed fraction; heavy variance across customers could change tail behavior.
- Accounting: how to attribute net burn to sales vs product for cross-charge transparency?

Next steps / owners:
- Build canonical PARAMS + scenario generator in sheet: Ethan Park by 2026-02-28.
- Wire a lightweight daily simulation pipeline from billing (sampled) to validate cohort distributions: Maya Alvarado by 2026-03-10.
- Run A/B salvage pricing experiment in one region: assign to Solutions Eng pilot customers: Liam O'Neill + Solutions Eng by 2026-04-01.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; the sheet should live alongside the larger capacity simulator (see linked GH PR) but be the "fast reasoning" artifact for product + finance conversations.
- Please edit PARAMS first to reflect any more accurate amortized cost numbers before re-running scenarios.

Appendix: quick sanity checks to include in the sheet:
- Totals row: sum(demand_raw) across 90d window should equal sum(cohort committed-hours over same window) +/- migration adjustments.
- If salvage_revenue > amortized_cost, flag this scenario (means we could re-sell more aggressively).
- Peak-idle > 30% should generate action flag.

End of doc.
